short: Workspace, query rounds and gate synthesis

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.GroverFindAll.gridQubits
lean.plain: Qubits for subsets, flags and archive
lean.annotation: The fixed-size walk uses $m(n+1)+kn$ qubits. For the increasing-width family, the working register can hold $L_{\max}m$ address-and-flag slots. At $(1024,512)$, the cap $L_{\max}=2$ gives $2560n+2048$ total qubits, while one oracle round still acts on 1,024 slots.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.groverFindAll_rel_cost
lean.plain: Find-All round bound for large domains
lean.annotation: The theorem uses `CostModel.ofEmbeddedOracle`, which counts a whole parallel query as one operation. A gate bound would also have to account for the elementary operations implementing the unitaries between queries. That gate decomposition is outside the cost statement here.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.DickeSol.eigProj
lean.plain: Johnson eigenspace projectors from subset inclusion
lean.annotation: The recursion constructs the exact projectors used by the ideal walk. Under $2M\le N$ the checked projector products are zero across distinct degrees, so assigning signs by degree gives a reflection. The paper’s QSVT approximation error concerns synthesis of the reflection into gates. Probability-one correctness here refers to the ideal program.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.groverFindAnyProgram
lean.annotation: The joint reflection about the uniform state on all $mn$ address qubits is one allowed $S$-independent step. The wrapper translates it to a `QProg.qAssign` of an ideal unitary. The resource predicate counts query rounds, so a gate decomposition of the reflection is a separate calculation.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.groverFindAllProgram
lean.annotation: In the fixed-size Johnson construction, an isometry $J$ embeds the subset coordinates in the work register. Lean lifts an orthogonal subset operator $D$ by $I+J(D-I)J^{\mathsf T}$, which acts as $D$ on those coordinates and as the identity on their orthogonal complement. The program uses the resulting ideal unitary as an assignment.

lean.name: OracleDynamicCircuit.compile
lean.plain: Translation from oracle circuits to quantum programs
lean.annotation: The `.step s` case calls the translation `compileStep s` supplied by the caller. The Grover wrappers supply `QProg.qAssign`, so compilation here means translation to the program semantics with ideal unitary assignments.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.DickeSol.eigProj
lean.plain: Johnson eigenspace projectors from subset inclusion
lean.annotation: The inclusion matrix maps between consecutive subset sizes. On degree $j$, the polar step normalizes its transpose by the inverse square root of $(M+1-j)(N-M-j)$. Under $2(M+1)\le N$ this gives an isometry $\Psi$. The projector recurrence uses $\Psi P_j\Psi^{\mathsf T}$ and adds the complement $I-\Psi\Psi^{\mathsf T}$.
